venue_or_publisher: Morgan Stanley (relayed by Invezz, Benzinga, XTB)

key_findings: Software team: 'peak uncertainty has severely impacted Software multiples'; sector about 33% below Oct 2025; AI does not replace existing systems and could add about USD 400 billion to enterprise software by 2028 (Weiss); normalization could be sharp over 2-6 quarters (July 2026).
key_quote_with_page: Not quoted (snippet).
stance(supports/challenges/mixed/neutral: challenges (replacement); buy-side/sell-side divergence

authors: Kent Bennett; Talia Goldberg; Janelle Teng Wade; Sameer Dholakia and others (Bessemer Venture Partners)
title: The State of AI 2025
method_and_data: VC report: benchmarks of 20 AI startups plus market maps; section 'Systems of Record under pressure'. Investor with AI portfolio (interest).
key_findings: 'Those moats are degrading': AI structures unstructured data and generates code on demand, so migrating off a system of record is 'faster, cheaper, and more feasible than ever'; new CRM/ERP entrants (Day.ai, Attio, Everest, Doss, Rillet); SaaS giants 'waking up' (Intercom's USD 100M+ AI product); general LLM assistants at about 600M (ChatGPT) and 400M (Gemini) weekly users for daily tasks 'and creation'.
key_quote_with_page: "Now, those moats are degrading. With AI's ability to structure unstructured data and generate code on demand, migrating to a new system is faster, cheaper, and more feasible than ever." (web, section III)
theory_or_lens: Switching-cost erosion; replacement N1 for systems of record
stance(supports/challenges/mixed/neutral: supports (N1/N4 for systems of record): the opposite of the IDC and Bain stance
notes: The VC view that systems of record are the vulnerable layer contradicts the analyst view that they are safe. Bessemer's State of the Cloud 2024 and any 2026 edition were NOT found open.

title: 2026 State of AI Report: The Builder's Economy
method_and_data: Survey of 300+ executives at software companies building AI products; full report behind a form.
key_findings: AI products 32% of revenue in 2025 to a projected 42% in 2026; gross margins 45% to 53% projected; consumption pricing share rose 35% to 42% and outcome-based 18% to 23% in six months; average 1.7 pricing models blended; subscriptions still most common; Anthropic most-cited model provider (81%).
key_quote_with_page: "Subscriptions remain most common, but consumption-based pricing rose from 35% to 42% in six months, and outcome-based from 18% to 23%." (web)
stance(supports/challenges/mixed/neutral: mixed (pricing is being rebuilt, subscription persists)
notes: Sample is builders of AI products, many AI-native: not representative of incumbents. Seat-share figure (23%) in podcast blurbs not verified and not used.

title: Is Software Losing Its Head?
method_and_data: VC essay on 'headless' systems of record after Salesforce's April 2026 announcement to open APIs; investor with portfolio interests.
key_findings: 'In the SaaS era, the system of record was defensible because humans lived in the interface. In the agentic era, that advantage weakens.' Defensibility shifts down (data models, permissions, workflow logic, compliance) and up (networks, proprietary data generation, real-world execution). 'The UI was the product.' Salesforce's 'headless' launch is called a repositioning with APIs that 'have largely existed for years'.
key_quote_with_page: "In the SaaS era, the system of record was defensible because humans lived in the interface. In the agentic era, that advantage weakens." (web)
stance(supports/challenges/mixed/neutral: supports (N3: the UI moat disappears when agents are the user)
notes: Directly relevant to creation tools, whose product IS the interface (canvas, editor). The essay concerns systems of record only; the extension to creation UIs is an inference to be tested.

authors: Gio Ahern; Stephenie Zhang; Alex Immerman (a16z)
title: From 'System of Record' to 'System of Intelligence'
method_and_data: VC essay using the news-feed analogy and a GTM survey (not fully seen).
key_findings: The CRM 'isn't going to go away' but becomes 'one of many inputs' into systems of intelligence; users were 'hostages, not customers' (Rampell); next decade's GTM enterprise value accrues to the reasoning layer above the database, which treats the database as infrastructure.
key_quote_with_page: "In the next decade, you want to own the system of intelligence that pulls from the system of record, becomes the user's one-stop shop for gaining context and taking action, and turns the SoR into something that's primarily consumed at the API layer." (web)
stance(supports/challenges/mixed/neutral: supports (N3)
notes: Pair with Activant (SP034), which traces the same SoR to SoI thesis to Jan 2025.

title: Software Isn't Dead. What's Valuable Is Changing.
method_and_data: VC essay with a three-tier value model (data/system of record, workflows, automation); one public-company statistic (median R&D about 24% of revenue).
key_findings: The sell-off is 'largely deserved' for CRUD-interface vendors but 'software is dead misses the mark': 'Code replicability was never the moat'; 'Software isn't stored code, it's embedded judgment'; taste, brand, customer success and trust do not get easier to replicate; systems of record 'prove to be increasingly valuable' but must capture richer context.
key_quote_with_page: "Software isn't stored code, it's embedded judgment." (web)
stance(supports/challenges/mixed/neutral: challenges (software death) while accepting repricing of CRUD products
notes: Taste and brand as moats are the creation-tool-relevant part of the argument; no creation tool is analysed.

title: Software is Dead?! Death by a thousand cuts (Software is dead | Long live software)
method_and_data: Investor research PDF (19 pages): index of 77 public software companies (down more than 20% since Nov 2025; median 3.6x EV/NTM revenue, 60% below long-term average) plus literature on AI and employment.
key_findings: Four simultaneous 'cuts': seats contract, 'all software gets vibe-coded', intensified competition, disintermediation. Seat-based pricing 'prevents traditional software companies from participating in the upside of AI adoption' (GitLab: deployments per user +35-45% yet slowest growth and NRR 118%). Seats still growing at Salesforce and ServiceNow; contraction expected slower than priced. First public thoughts on SoR to SoI shift dated Jan 2025.
key_quote_with_page: "The real risk for SaaS that we see: death by a thousand cuts." (p. 2)
theory_or_lens: Multi-factor disruption; N2, N4, N3 combined
stance(supports/challenges/mixed/neutral: mixed (disruption real, speed overstated)
notes: Cites Nadella's collapse remark as the opening evidence. Best single typology of risks in the VC literature. Claims about labour-market studies are the authors' citations, not verified here.

title: AI leads a service as software paradigm shift
method_and_data: VC essay sizing a USD 4.6 trillion opportunity (USD 2.3 trillion salaries in sales/marketing, software engineering, security and HR, plus USD 2.3 trillion outsourced IT and business-process services, per Gartner).
key_findings: Origin of 'service-as-software': in software, 'customers are still responsible for using that tool to achieve the desired outcome'; in services responsibility for the outcome sits with the seller. 'Instead of QuickBooks, you offer tax services.' Salesforce's USD 35 billion revenue is small beside USD 1.1 trillion of sales and marketing salaries.
key_quote_with_page: "Instead of QuickBooks, you offer tax services, in this case conducted by an AI accountant." (web)
stance(supports/challenges/mixed/neutral: supports (N6: software revenue pools expand into labour spend)
notes: Earliest of the 'services as software' framings (before Sequoia 2026, G13). Sizing by addition of salary and outsourcing spend is a TAM argument, not evidence. Update 'lessons from year one' (2025) not opened.

title: AI's $600B Question
method_and_data: Essay computing the revenue needed to justify AI infrastructure capex (Nvidia run-rate revenue scaled up); not about SaaS.
key_findings: Infrastructure spend implies a gap of roughly USD 600 billion between capex and end-user AI revenue (follow-up to AI's $200B question, Sept 2023).
key_quote_with_page: Not quoted (snippet).
stance(supports/challenges/mixed/neutral: neutral
notes: Included because the stream brief names it; it does NOT address SaaS. Sequoia's relevant piece is 'Services: The New Software' (G13, March 2026).

title: Clouded Judgement 2.13.26: Build vs Buy
method_and_data: Practitioner newsletter, weekly public SaaS comps; this issue is an argument.
key_findings: Rejects 'everyone will vibe-code their own software' (total cost of ownership, speed, focus, maintenance, scale, compliance). The real risk: 'The cost of creating software is going to zero', so ten new CRMs built for agents and priced on consumption flood the market and legacy software commoditises, to be valued as post-growth. 'People are simultaneously under and over estimating' AI's impact: over in the short term, under in the long term.
key_quote_with_page: "The cost of creating software is going to zero." (web)
stance(supports/challenges/mixed/neutral: mixed: rejects N1 build-your-own, endorses N4 commoditisation
notes: Frames the supervisor's 'anyone can do it' point precisely: it is entrants, not customers, who exploit falling build costs. Author affiliation not verified; treat as practitioner commentary.

title: The SaaS Rout of 2026 Is Even Worse Than You Think. For the First Time Ever, Software Now Trades at a Discount to the S&P 500
method_and_data: Practitioner blog citing software forward P/E by period (Bloomberg data per author).
key_findings: Median forward P/E: 84.1x (May 2020-May 2022), 43.2x (to June 2024), 33.6x (to June 2025), 31.2x (H2 2025), 22.7x (Jan-Mar 2026), below the S&P 500; IGV down over 21% YTD and about 30% from Sept 2025 peak (USD 2 trillion). Attributes the repricing to seat compression and private-credit worries.
key_quote_with_page: "Software forward P/E multiples have now fallen below the overall S&P 500." (web)
stance(supports/challenges/mixed/neutral: supports (market repricing); description, not explanation
notes: Practitioner (SaaS investor/event operator): numbers are the author's, sourced to Bloomberg without exhibit. Use with the Activant index and Goldman positioning.

title: Software Lost $300 Billion in a Day. Anthropic Was Just the Excuse.
method_and_data: Journalistic analysis using Bloomberg and market data.
key_findings: Argues the move priced margin compression and SaaS platform fatigue building since 2024, not AI extinction: ETF already -15% in January; five-year returns Salesforce -16%, Workday -37%, Adobe -44%; PE and BDC exposure to software doubled to 20% vs 10% in 2016; Goldman software basket -6% on the day.
key_quote_with_page: "Market is repricing margin compression, not AI extinction." (Breakdown, web)
stance(supports/challenges/mixed/neutral: challenges (AI as sole cause of the sell-off)
notes: Counter-explanation to the AI-causal reading; the USD 300 billion is a two-index figure, not comparable with other tallies.

key_quote_with_page: Summary: "Generative AI is poised to revolutionize enterprise software, transforming traditional workflow systems into dynamic, goal-oriented environments." (HBR summary, web)

title: AI's Impact on SaaS Will Be Uneven. Here's What Leaders Need to Know.
verification: [V-open: summary page, accessed 2026-11-14]; sample and results from search summaries only [V-snippet]
method_and_data: Academic-authored HBR article; (per snippets) analysis of 45 public SaaS companies from 10-Ks, classified by deterministic vs predictive tasks and internal vs pooled data; returns compared.
key_findings: Warns against overgeneralising from the SaaSpocalypse that most SaaS should be rebuilt internally. Snippets: predictive tools on pooled data outperformed deterministic internal-data tools by about 2 points a month since ChatGPT and fell about 4% vs 9% in the 2026 sell-off.
key_quote_with_page: Summary: "If AI can build or automate software, most SaaS should be rebuilt internally or..." (HBR summary, truncated, web)
theory_or_lens: Task and data typology of exposure
stance(supports/challenges/mixed/neutral: challenges (uniform disruption); heterogeneity by task and data
notes: Closest to an empirical academic test of exposure; results unverified until the full text is read. Type: HBR is practitioner outlet (GREY-B), author is a professor: coded here as GREY-B with academic authorship, NOT peer-reviewed.

authors: Sen Li; Xinying Qu; Rahul Divekar
title: How Generative AI Reshapes Business Models: A Review Through the Business Model Canvas
method_and_data: Review article using the Business Model Canvas; literature-based.
key_findings: GenAI should be managed 'as a system-level change, not just a new application'; pilots fail to scale because of poor integration, fragmented data, weak governance, misaligned incentives. Not specific to SaaS.
key_quote_with_page: "GenAI should be managed as a system-level change, not just a new application." (summary, web)
stance(supports/challenges/mixed/neutral: neutral (general business-model lens)
notes: Only CMR piece found on the topic; related CMR items Azabagic et al. 2026 and Pettersson et al. 2025 are already in the academic register (AI08, AI10). No CMR or MIT SMR article on SaaS disruption was found.

authors: David M. Rothschild; Jake M. Hofman; Markus Mobius; Brendan Lucier; Eleanor Dillon; Daniel G. Goldstein; Nicole Immorlica; Aleksandrs Slivkins
title: From Augmentation to Reconstruction: Guiding the AI Disruption to the Good Place
method_and_data: Conceptual economics paper: three-stage lens (augmentation, automation, reconstruction).
key_findings: The expected disruption 'has not fully arrived' mainly because organisations use AI to accelerate pre-AI workflows; the most consequential stage rebuilds workflows and markets around delegation and machine-to-machine interaction, requiring trust infrastructure, machine-legible data and interfaces, new workflows and incentives (complementary investments).
key_quote_with_page: "Artificial intelligence feels omnipresent, yet the disruption many expect has not fully arrived." (abstract)
theory_or_lens: Complementary investments; stages of AI adoption
stance(supports/challenges/mixed/neutral: supports N5 timing (slow, complementary-investment-bound) and the eventual N3 reconstruction
notes: Affiliation (Microsoft Research authors, per recall) not verified in the abstract. Offers theory for why incumbents get time and why the end-state is machine-to-machine.

title: Agentic Software: How AI Agents Are Restructuring the Software Paradigm
method_and_data: Conceptual paper on deterministic vs agentic software; historical arc.
key_findings: Traces licensed software to SaaS to Agent-as-a-Service; in agentic software 'the agent itself is the software' and decision logic is generated at runtime; each shift moves complexity from users to vendors, now including decision-making.
key_quote_with_page: "in the latter, the agent itself is the software, and its decision logic is generated at runtime." (abstract)
stance(supports/challenges/mixed/neutral: supports (N1)
notes: Single-author conceptual preprint; no data.

title: The Headless Firm: How AI Reshapes Enterprise Boundaries
method_and_data: Theoretical coordination-cost model with two falsifiable predictions; implications for software economics.
key_findings: Agentic protocols reduce integration cost from O(n^2) to O(n); selects an 'hourglass' structure: personalised generative interface on top, standardised protocol waist, market of micro-specialised execution agents below.
key_quote_with_page: "We argue that agentic AI induces a structural change in how coordination costs scale." (abstract)
theory_or_lens: Transaction/coordination cost theory of the firm
stance(supports/challenges/mixed/neutral: supports (N3: protocol waist, interface layer separated from execution)
notes: Complements register NEW02/NEW03 (Hydari and Muzaffar). Employer of authors not verified.

title: Decommissioning Enterprise Software: AI Agents and the Collapse of the Replication Moat
method_and_data: Practitioner-author working paper; three October 2026 cases of rebuilt software, economics, law, security by obscurity.
key_findings: One developer with an AI assistant can rebuild the part of a product a business actually uses in weeks; 'the industry can no longer charge people for how hard it is to leave'; not 'software has lost its value'.
key_quote_with_page: "I am saying the industry can no longer charge people for how hard it is to leave." (abstract)
stance(supports/challenges/mixed/neutral: supports (N4 and a limited N1)
notes: Single author (self-described developer), anecdotal cases; low rigour. Illustrates the 'replication moat' argument only.

title: Are B2B Software Vendors Readable by AI Assistants? Evidence from 251 Homepages
method_and_data: Descriptive audit of 274 B2B software homepages (251 readable): llms.txt, JSON-LD, robots.txt AI-crawler rules, composite score 0-100.
key_findings: Median readiness 75; sales and marketing software median 93, productivity and collaboration software median 55.5 and blocks AI crawlers most (14%); AI-native vendors in bottom half; 60.6% publish llms.txt.
key_quote_with_page: "Readiness varies by category: sales and marketing software has a median of 93, while productivity and collaboration software has a median of 55.5 and blocks crawlers most often (14% of sites)." (abstract)
stance(supports/challenges/mixed/neutral: neutral (empirical evidence on agent-readiness; productivity tools lag)
notes: Rare data point that isolates productivity and collaboration tools. Sample is B2B homepages, not product APIs; preprint, unreviewed. Connects to IDC 'if an agent cannot find your capability' (G05).

title: The Outcome Economy: A Business Model Design Framework for the Post-SaaS Era of Autonomous AI Agents
method_and_data: Conceptual framework with one self-operated implementation (BossFood).
key_findings: Thesis: 'SaaS does not die, it regresses to infrastructure' while an Outcome-as-a-Service layer captures value and the customer relationship; 'Outcome Capture Principle': when the marginal cost of capability approaches zero, value migrates to whoever guarantees the result.
key_quote_with_page: "SaaS does not die, it regresses to infrastructure." (abstract)
stance(supports/challenges/mixed/neutral: supports (N6)
notes: Non-peer-reviewed conceptual paper by an implementer; the implementation is the author's own. Useful only as an explicit statement of the rival hypothesis R-outcome.

title: Pricing and Competition in Generative AI Ecosystems
method_and_data: Analytical model of a two-tier value chain (upstream token pricing, downstream subscription).
key_findings: With usage-based upstream fees and subscription downstream, equilibrium prices, coverage and profits depend on usage heterogeneity; conditions for double marginalisation and demand distortion.
key_quote_with_page: "A key feature of this emerging ecosystem is a vertical pricing mismatch where upstream Gen AI service providers typically charge usage-based (token-based) fees, while downstream AI application providers rely on subscription pricing for end users." (abstract)
stance(supports/challenges/mixed/neutral: neutral (formal model of the incumbent's cost squeeze)
notes: Theory counterpart to Canva's cost shock (SP052). Related to register NEW09 (Mahmood), NEW10-NEW12.

title: "Job Envelope" Pricing Framework for AI Agents: A Comparative Perspective with Electricity, Telecom and Cloud Pricing Evolution
method_and_data: Conceptual comparison with historical utility, telecom and cloud tariffs; proposes a three-part tariff (envelope fee, allowance, quality modifiers).
key_findings: Usage- or outcome-based pricing fails to capture agent cost structures; multi-part tariffs converge as technologies commoditise.
key_quote_with_page: "This paper proposes pricing per job envelope as a new paradigm for AI agents." (abstract)
stance(supports/challenges/mixed/neutral: neutral
notes: Journal quality not assessed (new outlet); use cautiously.

title: Market Reactions to Generative AI Announcements: An Event Study Analysis of Abnormal Returns, 2022-2025
venue_or_publisher: Journal of Economic Research & Reviews (22 Jun 2026)
method_and_data: Event study: six AI-linked equities (Nvidia, Microsoft, Alphabet, Meta, AMD, Palantir), 18 announcements, Nov 2022 to Jan 2025.
key_findings: Announcement-day abnormal returns average +1.84% (significant) with day +1 drift (+0.71%): markets react fast but incompletely.
key_quote_with_page: "Markets react fast and in the right direction, with announcement-day abnormal returns averaging +1.84%" (abstract)
stance(supports/challenges/mixed/neutral: neutral (method template; wrong population)
notes: Shows the method but covers AI winners, not SaaS. NO event study of SaaS stocks around Cowork plugins (30 Jan to 3 Feb 2026) or Claude Design (17 Apr 2026) was found: a gap and a possible methodological contribution.

authors: Mia Osmonbekov (Fortune); quoting Melanie Perkins, Derek Hernandez (PitchBook)

key_findings: Canva cut expected 2026 growth by a third to 20% as AI feature costs exceeded plan; cost per task cut nearly 90% since Canva AI 2.0 (April); users create 3x as many designs; 'AI is making SaaS no longer a zero marginal cost solution' (PitchBook); Figma's 'shrinking margins' cited as the same problem.
key_quote_with_page: "AI is making SaaS no longer a zero marginal cost solution, which has really been what I would call a lot of software's secret sauce up until now." (Derek Hernandez, PitchBook, web)
stance(supports/challenges/mixed/neutral: supports (cost-of-AI thread of the debate: demand for AI exceeds economics)
notes: Opened here although casi/canva.md records Fortune as 403: upgrade that reference to V-open. Creation-tool evidence that the threat is also internal (cost), not only external (replacement).

key_findings: Despite record Q1 FY26 revenue (USD 6.40 billion) shares fell as 'investors worry that fast-moving AI agents and other new tools could weaken demand for parts of the traditional seat-based software model'; Adobe must keep pace without alienating artists or enterprise trust ('moving at 100 miles an hour' vs customers 'at 10').
key_quote_with_page: "The fastest moving AI models and the AI companies, let's say they're moving at 100 miles an hour. The customers are moving at 10 miles an hour." (Anil Chakravarthy, Adobe, web)
stance(supports/challenges/mixed/neutral: supports (N2 applied to a creation incumbent)

title: The Effect of AI Agents on Switching Costs: How Another Moat in Banking Is Being Filled
method_and_data: Empirical baseline with FFIEC and NCUA data on rate-driven deposit switching; analogy to Yu'e Bao in China.
key_findings: Effort-based switching costs historically suppress rate-driven switching only modestly (0.40-0.66 pp of deposit share per pp of rate spread); agents may drive effort cost toward zero.
